def estimate_tokens(text):
    return max(1, len(text) // 4)

def trim_to_budget(messages, budget):
    """Keep messages[0] (system) plus the newest turns that fit in budget."""
    system, rest = messages[0], messages[1:]
    used = estimate_tokens(system["content"])
    kept = []
    for m in reversed(rest):
        cost = estimate_tokens(m["content"])
        if used + cost > budget:
            break
        kept.append(m)
        used += cost
    kept.reverse()
    return [system] + kept

messages = [
    {"role": "system", "content": "Be brief."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "My name is Arun and I live in Madurai."},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "Hello Arun."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "What is a tuple?"},
    {"role": "assistant", "content": "An immutable sequence."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "And a list?"},
]
for m in trim_to_budget(messages, budget=16):
    print(m["role"], "|", m["content"])

import re

STOPWORDS = {"the", "a", "an", "is", "are", "i", "my", "me", "do", "how", "what", "to", "in", "of"}

def keywords(text):
    return {w for w in re.findall(r"[a-z0-9.]+", text.lower()) if w not in STOPWORDS}

def recall(notes, query, k=2):
    """Return up to k notes with the most keyword overlap; ties alphabetical."""
    q = keywords(query)
    scored = [(len(q & keywords(n)), n) for n in notes]
    scored = [pair for pair in scored if pair[0] > 0]
    scored.sort(key=lambda pair: (-pair[0], pair[1]))
    return [n for _, n in scored[:k]]

notes = [
    "User name is Arun, based in Madurai.",
    "User prefers tabs over spaces.",
    "Favourite editor is VS Code.",
    "Arun is learning about tuples and lists.",
]
print(recall(notes, "What editor does the user prefer?"))
print(recall(notes, "Remind me what Arun is learning"))
print(recall(notes, "Hello there"))
